songs.name: I've Been All Around This World

ai_show_review.summary: Acoustic gems with Black Peter & Lovelight, marred by guest vocals
ai_show_review.blurb: The set shines on the acoustic numbers, delivering a moving Black Peter and a bright Turn On Your Lovelight after Not Fade Away. Jerry’s vocal tone is sweet and heartbreaking, Bob’s voice crystal clear, and the drums stay tight. The surprise guest on the final three songs disrupts momentum and leaves the closing feeling uneven.
ai_show_review.review:
On March 8, 1970 at Phoenix’s Travelodge Theatre in the Round, the Dead offered a tightly‑crafted acoustic‑heavy set that still resonates for its intimate moments. Early numbers flow into a heartfelt rendition of “Black Peter,” where Jerry Garcia’s vocal tone is described as sweet and heartbreaking, complemented by an acoustic guitar solo that shines through the soundboard capture. The band rides the momentum straight into a spirited “Turn On Your Lovelight*” after a chaotic but energetic “Not Fade Away*,” showcasing crystal‑clear vocals from Bob Weir and rock‑solid drumming from Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann. While Pigpen’s keyboards sit in the mix, an unexpected guest vocalist on the final three numbers (including another “Not Fade Away*”) introduces volume spikes and vocal disruptions that pull the show’s momentum down, leaving listeners with a mixed impression of the closing segment.

Overall, the performance is a solid snapshot of the early‑70 Dead—tight rhythm section, emotive acoustic storytelling, and moments of brilliance—but it’s softened by the ill‑timed guest appearance. For fans seeking the purest listening experience, the “gd70-03-08.sbd.9195.sbeok.shnf” soundboard recording delivers the clearest capture of these highlights while still exposing the occasional vocal hiccup.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard source that captures the acoustic set clearly and highlights Black Peter and Lovelight, while remaining the most listenable despite guest vocal issues.

key_highlights: Exquisite acoustic rendition of “Black Peter” with heartfelt vocals.
Bright transition from “Not Fade Away*” into a lively “Turn On Your Lovelight*”.
Tight drum work provides a solid rhythmic foundation throughout.
Guest vocalist on the final three songs creates volume spikes and disrupts momentum.

band_performance.Jerry: Sweet, heartbreaking vocal delivery on Black Peter and a praised acoustic guitar solo.
band_performance.Phil: Bass remains steady and supportive, anchoring the acoustic set.
band_performance.Bob: Crystal‑clear vocals that enhance the overall sound, especially on Lovelight.
band_performance.Pigpen: Keyboard and harmonica parts sit unobtrusively in the mix; no standout moments noted.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are tight, providing a solid rhythmic foundation throughout the show.
band_performance.Billy: Drumming stays locked in with Mickey, reinforcing the band’s steady groove.
